title: The Sun-Baked Arch
story:
The trail through the Golden Valley Scrubland wound like a pale ribbon across rolling hills of amber grass. The morning air was dry and crisp, smelling of warmed earth and dusty sun. James set a steady pace, the brass map canister brushing against his flank with every step, its leather strap bound with Mateo's colorful threads catching the vibrant sunlight.

He walked past dry stands of broad blue agave standing like spiky guards along the path. He walked past low, crumbling field walls built by hands long forgotten. He walked past flat limestone boulders where small grey lizards basked under the open sky. Every few hundred paces, he checked the needle of his small brass compass, watching it settle faithfully toward the south.

By late afternoon, the scrubland opened into a wide, quiet plateau anchored by a solitary limestone archway. Half-buried in wild dry grass, the arch had stood against the mountain wind for generations, its hand-carved surfaces smoothed away by time. James scrambled up the warm, sun-baked stone, perching at the top to look out over the vast expanse before him.

Holding his smooth piece of green sea-glass to his eye, he watched the golden hills transform into a quiet sea of emerald hue. He thought of the high trees of the Great Canopy, the winding canals of Oakhaven, and the sweet smell of cedar shavings from Don Tadeo's shop, marveling at how each place had given him a piece of home. As the sun dipped behind the western hills, painting the sky in soft violet and amber, James nestled into a dry, sheltered nook at the base of the arch, content to listen to the whisper of the night wind through the grass.
